newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU to put tough conditions on Thomson - papers.
newsitem.headline: EU to put tough conditions on Thomson - papers.

text.p: The European Union Commission will attach tough conditions to any approval for an 11-billion franc ($2.1 billion) capital injection into state-owned defence and consumer electronics group Thomson SA, French newspapers reported on Monday.
Les Echos and La Tribune said that the EU would demand a freeze on production volumes, a freeze on market share as well as a detailed recovery plan before giving its go-ahead.
But Liberation said that the EU would allow the sale of Thomson to Lagardere Groupe and Daewoo Electronics on Wednesday December 4.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis is in Brussels on Monday to give the commission additional information about the privatisation process of Thomson.
A commission meeting on December 18 is scheduled to take a decision on the state-aid, the French papers said.
If the European Commission does give the two green lights, France's Privatisation Commission can render its decision before the end of the year.

If the EU wants further information, or wants to start a detailed inquiry, the procedure could be delayed and go past the December 31 validity date for the original Lagardere and Alcatel Alsthom offers.
Alcatel has said it is ready to make a fresh offer after December 31.

The Le Monde newspaper on Saturday published what it said was a working paper dated November 26 from commissioner Karel van Miert, in which he warned France he needed all information by December 2 or else the procedure could be delayed.
